title: Friction and Brakes
objective: After this level you can explain friction and how brakes stop a moving car.
summary: Friction resists sliding and turns motion into heat. Brakes use it on purpose, and since doubling speed quadruples the energy of motion, it quadruples braking distance.

cards.headline: Double your speed, and your car needs four times as far to brake.
cards.body: Not twice as far: four times, with the same brakes pressing just as hard. The reason is energy, and the force that has to get rid of it is friction.

cards.headline: Friction: surfaces that catch
cards.body: Friction is a force that resists one surface sliding over another. Even surfaces that feel smooth are rough up close, and their bumps catch. Starting something sliding takes more force than keeping it going, which is why a heavy box suddenly lurches once it finally moves. Friction is also what lets your shoes grip the floor. Without it, every walk would be an ice rink.

cards.headline: Brakes turn motion into heat
cards.body: A disc brake is friction on purpose. Pads press against a metal disc that turns with the wheel, and the rubbing slows it. Level 2's rule decides where the car's energy of motion goes: it can't vanish, so it becomes heat in the brakes. Rub your hands together fast and you can feel the same trick, just smaller.

cards.fact: Twice the speed means four times the energy of motion to get rid of.
cards.context: A car at 100 km/h carries four times the energy of motion it has at 50 km/h. Brakes pressing equally hard remove it at a steady rate per meter, so the braking distance quadruples too. Level 25's regenerative braking saves some of that energy as electricity; friction brakes can only turn it into heat.

mascot.line: That's why 'just a little faster' is never just a little. Your brakes do the maths even when you don't.

A kind of energy stored inside rough objects
options.rationale: Friction is a force, not stored energy.

options.rationale: Gravity pulls down; friction resists sliding.

options.label: The push that a spark gives to an engine piston

questions.explanation: Friction is a force that resists one surface sliding over another, because rough surfaces catch.

questions.prompt: A car doubles its speed. With the same brakes pressing just as hard, how far does it now need to brake?

options.label: The same distance
options.rationale: The car carries far more energy of motion.

options.label: Twice as far
options.rationale: Energy of motion grows faster than speed.

options.label: Eight times as far
options.rationale: Doubling speed quadruples the energy, not eightfold.

questions.explanation: Doubling speed gives four times the energy of motion, so steady braking needs four times the distance.

questions.prompt: How does Level 25's regenerative braking differ from an ordinary friction brake?

options.label: It stops the car without slowing the wheels
It saves some energy as electricity instead of heat
It creates new energy while braking
It works only on gas cars
options.rationale: It needs a motor that can act as a generator.

questions.explanation: Friction brakes turn the energy of motion into heat; regenerative braking turns some of it into electricity for the battery.
